clue.text: Mistress and mother triumphed outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for triumphed wraps around the word for mother

parts.note: triumphed means won
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A lady of the house and her mother have come out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistress' tempts as a lover, but here it is simply the dated sense of a lady; 'outside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress is a dated term for a woman, especially one in charge of a household.

clue.text: Astounding flow under construction

indicators.note: construction suggests the letters are being built into a new form

explanation.surface: A remarkable stream is still being built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under construction' reads as one phrase, but 'under' is part of the anagram fodder with FLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wonderful is amazing or astonishing, a synonym of astounding.

clue.text: Pliant kid makes very strong ale

definitions.meaning: an exceptionally strong old ale brewed at Levens Hall in Cumbria

explanation.surface: A supple young goat produces potent beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' is the leather, not a child or young goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is fine soft goatskin leather, and was also the name of a famously potent ale.

clue.text: Cosy home in Tyneside street

parts.note: Tyneside is in north-east England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A snug house in a road in Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a snug, comfortable home, used figuratively of a cosy dwelling.

clue.text: Stop paper coming out before hospital closure

indicators.note: before places the hospital letter ahead of the word for closure
coming out suggests the letters of paper emerge in a new arrangement

parts.note: a closure is an end

explanation.surface: A newspaper's publication is held up before a hospital is shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' is the anagram signal, suggesting a paper being published; 'Stop' means arrest, not halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprehend a suspect is to stop and arrest them, a synonym in the police sense.

clue.text: Nick Guest?

parts.note: nick is slang for jail, so a guest at the nick is someone calling on inmates

explanation.surface: A name, as if of a person called Nick Guest.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a person's name; 'nick' is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who calls on inmates is a guest at the jail, a visitor to the nick.

clue.text: This man was fine in Ireland

definitions.meaning: in old Irish law, a payment made by a killer to the victim's family

explanation.surface: This fellow paid a penalty over in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, and an old Irish blood-fine paid for a killing.

clue.text: One who forces payment from former player

parts.note: ex means former
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A one-time performer now demands money.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact payment is to demand it, so one who exacts is a demander of money.

clue.text: Duke discover quail?

parts.note: to read can mean to find out or learn, as in reading the news

explanation.surface: A nobleman finds a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quail' looks like the bird but is the verb, to shrink in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to cower in fear, and to dread is to fear greatly.

clue.text: Portia's waiting-maid retiring like a temptress

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the whole phrase is read backwards

parts.note: as means like
a siren is a seductive temptress

explanation.surface: A lady's maid is withdrawing in the manner of a seductress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns ASSIREN backwards. Nerissa is Portia's maid in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerissa is the name of Portia's companion and waiting-woman in Shakespeare's comedy set in Venice.

clue.text: Convex pie near-cooked, here in France

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are altered or falsified into a new order

explanation.surface: A bulging pie, nearly baked, sold in a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near-cooked' looks like one word but 'near' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Aix-en-Provence is a city in southern France, a place there.

clue.text: Parody within the limit at Eton…

indicators.note: within shows the answer is sitting inside the following run of words

explanation.surface: A send-up performed within the bounds of what Eton College will tolerate.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through limIT AT Eton. Eton is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: To parody someone is to imitate them, usually mockingly; both are verbs of copying.

clue.text: and the rest have to begin to eat out

parts.note: etc, short for et cetera, means and the rest

indicators.note: to begin points to the opening letter of the word have

explanation.surface: Continuing the Eton theme: everyone else must start by dining out.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 11-across with its leading dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid etches metal by eating away its surface, so eat out is a fair synonym.

clue.text: 9-1 on, he was bound to get hot

definitions.text: he was bound to get hot

parts.note: Roman numerals IX for nine and I for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse at nine to one on was certain to warm up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like betting odds. In Greek myth Ixion was bound to a fiery wheel for eternity.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus punished Ixion by tying him to a burning, spinning wheel, so he was bound to get hot.

clue.text: Boss of the breeding establishment

definitions.meaning: a boss is a raised knob or ornamental ...
a farm where horses are kept for breeding

explanation.surface: The man in charge of a farm where animals are bred.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a decorative knob on a surface, and a place keeping stallions for breeding.

clue.text: Article on head of Thomas Short, a musketeer

indicators.note: on head of puts the article on top of the abbreviation in this down entry

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
Thos is the short form of Thomas

explanation.surface: A grammatical article about a short man named Thomas the musketeer.
explanation.walkthrough: Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Athos is one of the three musketeers in Alexandre Dumas's famous novel.

clue.text: Reportedly remained sober

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for remained is heard rather than seen

parts.note: stayed means remained

explanation.surface: Apparently he stayed on and kept a straight face.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid means serious and sedate, a near synonym of sober in manner.

clue.text: But he does not make his mark at sea

definitions.text: But he does not make his mark at sea

parts.words: But he does not make his mark at sea
parts.note: read as an undecided elector who has not yet put a cross on the ballot, all at sea as in uncertain

explanation.surface: A sailor who fails to leave any impression on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' means undecided, and 'make his mark' is putting a cross on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter not committed to any party drifts between them, undecided at election time.

clue.text: Coast clear, taking a turn

parts.note: free means clear, as in free of obstacles
a wheel is a turning movement, as in a right wheel

explanation.surface: The seaside is open, and the road bends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coast' looks like the seaside but is the verb, to roll without pedalling.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast on a bicycle is to freewheel, moving without pedalling.

clue.text: Stall? Pierrots can, at resort

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: Seaside clowns at a holiday resort can delay things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like the seaside setting for pierrots, a traditional seaside clown act; read as re-sort it rearranges PIERROTS CAN AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to play for time, putting off action, which is to delay.

clue.text: Settle buyer's option to get inactive medicine

parts.note: to settle something in position is to place it
BO is the abbreviation for buyer's option

explanation.surface: Settling on a choice of a dummy drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy medicine with no active ingredient.

clue.text: Silver bullet stuck in the bank

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a round is a bullet or cartridge

explanation.surface: A silver bullet lodged in a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a sandbank, not a money bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship aground has run onto a sandbank or shore and is stuck there.

clue.text: Standard to drive at?

definitions.meaning: standard as in average or ordinary
what one is driving at is what one intends or signifies

explanation.surface: A norm to aim for when driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean is the average (a standard), and to mean something is what you are driving at.

clue.text: Gong struck, dead in the middle of dinner, say

indicators.note: in the middle of places the dead abbreviation inside the word for dinner

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: A dinner gong was struck while someone lay dead mid-meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gong' is British slang for a medal; 'struck' is a link, as medals are struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a medal or decoration.

clue.text: Egg-shaped tub in old English

indicators.note: in places the word for tub inside the old English abbreviation

parts.note: a vat is a large tub

explanation.surface: An egg-like barrel described in Anglo-Saxon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovate comes from Latin ovum, egg, and describes an oval shape broader at one end.

clue.text: Make sketch of daughter, undressed

parts.note: raw means undressed, as in unprocessed or without dressing

explanation.surface: An artist sketches his daughter in the nude.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something is to make a sketch of it with pencil or pen.

clue.text: Island destination of royal speedboat?

definitions.meaning: an island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland
speed, bonny boat, carrying Bonnie Prince Charlie over the sea

explanation.surface: Where a royal motorboat is headed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Skye Boat Song tells of Bonnie Prince Charlie fleeing by boat 'over the sea' in 1746.
explanation.definitionFit: An island of the Scottish Hebrides, famed as the boat song's destination.

clue.text: Naughty child's endless swindle

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A naughty child's never-ending con trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme or fraud, a synonym for swindle.

clue.text: Hide from complete family

parts.note: does means completes, as in does the job
kin means family

explanation.surface: Hiding away from one's entire family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the noun, an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Doeskin is the skin of a female deer, a type of hide or leather.

clue.text: He is alone in respect of clues to be worked out

parts.note: re means concerning or in respect of

indicators.note: to be worked out suggests the letters need solving into a new order

explanation.surface: A lonely solver with clues still to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be worked out' rearranges CLUES into CLUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse is a person who lives in seclusion, always alone.

clue.text: Album for the autumn?

parts.note: an album of detachable pages, whimsically linked to the season when foliage drops from trees

explanation.surface: A scrapbook suitable for the fall season.
explanation.walkthrough: An album with removable pages is described by a word that also suggests autumn foliage falling free.
explanation.definitionFit: A binder with detachable sheets is described by this term, suggesting falling foliage.

clue.text: Ideal fashion, long at the back

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style

indicators.note: at the back points to the final letter of the word long

explanation.surface: The perfect style has length at the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A model citizen is an ideal one, a perfect example to copy.
